title: From Mixture of Experts to Mixture of Agents with Super Fast Inference - Daniel Kim & Daria Soboleva
talk_summary: The talk explains mixture-of-experts, then demos mixture-of-agents: parallel specialist LLM calls, critique/filtering, and a summarizer, using Cerebras fast inference. Most content is Cerebras hardware marketing, but the multi-agent layering, automated grader, and agent-count cautions are transferable.

takeaways.technique: Layered parallel agent ensemble with sequential aggregation
takeaways.what_they_do: They configure layers of agents; agents within a layer run in parallel, their outputs are concatenated into the next layer, and a final summarization model aggregates the result.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Layer is a sequential but at each layer models are process in parallel.
takeaways.numbers: 3 layers; one demo used 500,000 tokens and 32 LLM calls

takeaways.what_they_do: A planning agent emits multiple candidate answers, a critique agent filters feasibility, and a summarization agent combines the best candidates into the final answer.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a critique agent comes in and be like, Hey, are these any of them feasible answers to this particular problem
takeaways.numbers: 8 proposals; 16k context of thinking tokens; 2 top answers; 32 LLM calls; 500,000 tokens

takeaways.technique: Automated grader for agent configuration tuning
takeaways.what_they_do: They give participants an automated grader that scores generated code up to 120 points, then have them tune model choice, temperature, prompts, and layer count against that score.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your goal is to configure your AI agent like mixture of agents system to automatically generate code that scores the maximum 120 points in our automated grader
takeaways.numbers: 120-point grader; baseline C; changing main model to Qwen improved to B

takeaways.what_they_do: They use multiple non-frontier/open models with specialized prompts and aggregation to outperform frontier models on some hard tasks, but note this requires prompt/system tuning.
takeaways.evidence_quote: take advantage of non-frontier models, even open source models that may not perform as well on benchmarks, and turn them into performing better than frontier models
takeaways.numbers: 7.4 seconds vs 293 seconds for a reasoning model; 500,000 tokens and 32 calls

takeaways.what_they_do: Each agent gets a custom system prompt focused on one part of the task, such as bug finding, performance optimization, or overall synthesis, instead of one generic reviewer.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're going to specialize each agent to solve a particular portion of the problem

takeaways.technique: Cap agent count to avoid redundancy
takeaways.what_they_do: They warn that too many agents create redundancy and extra time because not all agents contribute to the final answer; the number of agents/layers must be tuned.
